programs.name: Accelerate California (Central Valley iHub)
programs.short: State-funded inclusive innovation hub at the WET Center that connects Central Valley entrepreneurs, especially from underserved communities, with business support from partner SBDCs, lenders, chambers, and business centers.

programs.name: Accelerate California Inclusive Innovation Hub
programs.short: State-designated hub offering business advising, workshops, commercialization and R&D pathways, and investor connections for founders in rural Northern California, including agtech, clean energy, and health innovators.

programs.name: ADAPT (Advancing the Development of Agricultural workers' Proficiency with new Technologies)
programs.short: Training being developed by UC Davis's Western Center for Agricultural Health and Safety to prepare farmworkers to work with autonomous tractors, collaborative robots, agrivoltaics, and other emerging agricultural technologies.

programs.name: Adult Literacy Program
programs.short: English, math, financial, and computer literacy classes, including workplace math and Excel for supervisors, scheduled around vineyard work for Napa County farmworkers and their families.

programs.name: Advising Services
programs.short: Customized business advising that matches companies with advisors from the WET Center's network of industry experts, investors, and executives, based on each company's growth goals.

programs.name: Ag Learning to Lead (L2L)
programs.short: Support program for Hartnell agriculture students offering mentorship, tailored success support, and paid work-based learning to help them finish a certificate or degree or transfer to a university.

programs.name: Ag Technology & Mechatronics
programs.short: A full-day agriculture and FFA program in Salinas for young people without a high school diploma, combining academics with ag mechanics, irrigation and farm technology, drones, and industry certifications.

programs.name: Ag Technology Program
programs.short: Associate degree and certificates preparing students for technology-driven agriculture jobs, from field production and data management to automated processing and food safety, focused on the local fresh fruit industry.

programs.name: Ag-Tech Small Business Technical Assistance
programs.short: Business technical assistance for small agricultural and agtech businesses in the North State, such as customer and market research, funding research, websites, and marketing, delivered with regional partners.

programs.name: AgFunder Venture Investment
programs.short: AgFunder is a venture capital firm that invests mainly in seed and Series A startups using technologies such as artificial intelligence, robotics and biotechnology to solve problems in food, agriculture, health and climate.

programs.name: Aggie Square Industry Engagement (research space and core facility access)
programs.short: Approved companies and startups can locate in Aggie Square's Sacramento research laboratories and gain priority access to UC Davis research core facilities and collaboration with faculty; the district's focus is mainly life sciences.

programs.name: AgHiRE
programs.short: Hybrid leadership program for Spanish-speaking agricultural employees, supported by their employers. It covers leadership and communication, workplace English, digital skills, and workplace safety and labor rules.

programs.name: Agricultural Ambassadors
programs.short: A leadership program for Merced College agriculture students. Ambassadors build communication and leadership skills, plan events, lead tours and give presentations promoting agriculture education.

programs.name: Agricultural and Environmental Technology (B.S.)
programs.short: Undergraduate major in the College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences teaching students to apply data, robotics, digital tools, and AI to food, fiber, and energy production.

programs.name: Agricultural Business, B.S.
programs.short: Bachelor's degree in agricultural business, set up as a 2+2 pathway with community college agriculture courses. It covers management, marketing, finance, food safety and data analysis for food and fiber careers.

programs.name: Agricultural Mechatronics (AS and Foundation Certificate)
programs.short: Associate degree and certificate that prepare students to install, repair, and troubleshoot agricultural automation, robotics, and electromechanical systems, with chances to earn third-party industry certifications.

programs.name: Agriculture Business (A.S.-T and Agriculture Business Management Certificate)
programs.short: Transfer degree and certificate applying business and management concepts to agriculture, for students heading toward careers in farm operations, farm services, processing, marketing, and distribution of farm products.

programs.name: Agriculture Degrees and Certificates
programs.short: Associate degrees, transfer degrees, and certificates in agriculture business, plant science, production, and food safety that combine hands-on learning with preparation for agricultural careers or university transfer.

programs.name: Agriculture degrees and certificates
programs.short: Associate, transfer and certificate programs in agriculture business, animal science, crop and plant science, horticulture, equine science and agriculture education, with hands-on learning on the college farm, greenhouses and livestock facilities.

programs.name: Agriculture Plant Science (A.S.-T and Certificate)
programs.short: Associate degree for transfer and certificate applying biological and physical sciences to agriculture, preparing Imperial Valley students for CSU transfer or careers such as crop consultant, inspector, or farm manager.

programs.name: Agriculture Service Technology (A.S. and Certificate)
programs.short: Associate degree and certificate preparing students to maintain and repair agricultural and heavy equipment and automation systems, covering diesel engines, hydraulics and pneumatics, welding, industrial automation, and workplace safety.

programs.name: AgStart Office Hours
programs.short: One-on-one sessions that pair agriculture and food entrepreneurs with volunteer mentors to talk through business and technology needs, offered in person or remotely.

programs.name: AgSTEP Agriculture Systems Certificate
programs.short: A noncredit, competency-based community college certificate in which farmworkers and other agricultural learners build on skills they already have and gain agtech skills, with bilingual support and stackable pathways toward degrees.

programs.name: AgTEC Innovation Center
programs.short: Planned center at Reedley College that will host agricultural technology startups and give regional students internships, job shadows, and part-time work with them.

programs.name: AI Launchpad
programs.short: An applied AI, data science, and cloud computing program for high school and community college students, built on Central Valley weather, soil, and crop data and leading into F3i Data Challenges.

programs.name: Aldo Delfino Memorial Scholarship
programs.short: Scholarships from the Napa County Farm Bureau Foundation for high school seniors who plan to study agriculture in college.

programs.name: Angel Academy
programs.short: Cohort program with two paths: founders build and practice an investor pitch, while aspiring angel investors learn to evaluate early-stage companies; both meet at a closing live-pitch session.

programs.name: Bachelor of Science in Applied Agricultural Technology Systems (proposed)
programs.short: A proposed bachelor's degree that would combine agricultural technology and food systems education with applied workforce skills. It would be Merced College's first bachelor's degree.

programs.name: BizTech Connect
programs.short: Four-week virtual growth program with coaching on strategy, customer acquisition, operations, and financial planning for established, revenue-generating product companies in Inland Southern California.

programs.name: BlueTechValley Innovation Cluster
programs.short: California Energy Commission-supported innovation cluster managed by the WET Center, offering water, energy, and agtech startups legal, business, and technical help, pilot opportunities, and links to six CSU-based hubs.

programs.name: Build Career Pathways
programs.short: A year-long pathway in UX/UI design, digital marketing, web and software development, or IT where young adults build a professional portfolio with one-on-one coaching.

programs.name: Business Expansion and Site Selection Services
programs.short: Concierge support for companies moving to or growing in San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara counties, including site selection, business data, incentives, permitting connections, stakeholder introductions, and workforce training referrals.

programs.name: Business Location & Expansion Services
programs.short: Site selection, incentive navigation, custom research, hiring connections and partner introductions for companies, including agri-food tech firms, that are moving to, expanding in or staying in Greater Sacramento.

programs.name: Business Location and Expansion Services
programs.short: Help for businesses exploring a Fresno County location or expansion, including site selection, incentive and permitting guidance, utility cost analysis, financing referrals, and retention and growth support.

programs.name: Business Location and Resource Assistance
programs.short: Help from the City of Napa's Economic Development Division for businesses and developers looking to start, locate or grow in the city, including support with property searches, links to local business resources and real estate brokers, and information on developer incentives. The division also connects businesses with established local companies and development partners.

programs.name: Buy-Protect-Sell Pilot Program
programs.short: Ag + Open Space pilot that buys a farm or ranch, protects it with a conservation easement, and resells it to a qualified farmer or rancher seeking their own small or midsize property.

programs.name: CA GROWN Membership and Logo Licensing
programs.short: Membership in the Buy California Marketing Agreement and licensing of the CA GROWN logo. Lets California growers, commodity groups and ag businesses identify and promote their products as California grown.

programs.name: California Advanced Air Mobility Corridors Initiative (CAAMCI)
programs.short: A planned FAA-compliant flight corridor network linking Watsonville, Marina, Salinas, and Hollister airports where aviation and drone companies can test, certify, and commercialize aircraft, with applications including crop production.

programs.name: California Agricultural Workforce Development Program
programs.short: Connects agricultural employers, community colleges, and learners around technology skills, curriculum, training, and work experience.
programs.summary: CDFA’s Specialty Crop Workforce Development Program brings agricultural employers, community colleges, and other partners together around skills needed as farming adopts new technology. Regional partner connections help farmworkers and students find training routes, while employers and educators can discuss workforce needs and career pathways.

providers.name: California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA)

programs.name: California Business Investment Services (CalBIS)
programs.short: Confidential help for companies locating, expanding, or staying in California, including site selection, incentive navigation, and connections to state, local, and utility partners.

providers.name: California Governor’s Office of Business and Economic Development (GO-Biz)

programs.name: California Competes Tax Credit
programs.short: Competitive state income tax credit for businesses of any industry or size that commit to creating full-time jobs and investing in California, with GO-Biz staff available for application consultations.

providers.name: California Governor’s Office of Business and Economic Development (GO-Biz)

programs.name: California Farm Academy Courses
programs.short: Short hands-on courses and workshops for aspiring, beginning and experienced farmers on topics such as welding, tractor operation, irrigation, animal husbandry, farm business planning and marketing.

programs.name: California State Trade Expansion Program (STEP)
programs.short: Export assistance for California small businesses, including California pavilions at international trade shows and missions, export vouchers, and export training such as sector-focused market-entry programs.

providers.name: California Governor’s Office of Business and Economic Development (GO-Biz)

programs.name: California Underserved and Small Producer Program (CUSP)
programs.short: Direct relief grants for small, mid-sized, and socially disadvantaged California farmers and ranchers hurt by drought or extreme weather, with free application help from partner organizations.

providers.name: California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA)

programs.name: California Wine Grape Growers Foundation Scholarships
programs.short: Annual college scholarships for California high school seniors whose parent or guardian works for a winegrape grower, plus a memorial scholarship for Central Coast students studying viticulture or enology.

programs.name: CareerPoint Business Services: Hire Qualified Talent
programs.short: Recruiting help for North Bay businesses, including pre-screened candidate referrals, on-site recruiting events, job fairs, job postings, and answers to employment questions.

providers.name: Workforce Alliance of the North Bay

programs.name: CareerPoint Employer Training Services (On-the-Job, Incumbent Worker and Customized Training)
programs.short: Training support for North Bay employers, including on-the-job training with wage reimbursement, upskilling for current employees, and customized training developed with regional education providers.

providers.name: Workforce Alliance of the North Bay

programs.name: CareerPoint North Bay Career Centers
programs.short: Career centers in Lake, Marin, Mendocino and Napa counties offering career coaching, job search help, workshops, hiring events and referrals to training programs.

providers.name: Workforce Alliance of the North Bay

programs.name: CareerPoint Youth Services
programs.short: Career exposure for high school students through a network of volunteer professionals and career path tools, plus youth employment services through the CareerPoint centers.

providers.name: Workforce Alliance of the North Bay

programs.name: Center for Irrigation Technology Applied Research
programs.short: Applied research and technology transfer on irrigation efficiency, precision and variable-rate irrigation, and water and energy management, carried out with public and private collaborators; growers and companies can contact CIT to discuss projects.

programs.name: Center for Irrigation Technology Laboratory and Field Testing
programs.short: Independent third-party testing of irrigation products such as drip emitters, sprinklers, pumps, filters, valves, and soil-moisture controllers for manufacturers and technology developers who need performance data.

programs.name: CFMC Scholarships Program
programs.short: Scholarships that help graduating seniors from Merced County high schools pay for education after high school, including tuition, housing, books and supplies. Awards are usually paid directly to the student's school.

programs.name: ChicoSTART Co-Working
programs.short: Downtown Chico shared workspace with day passes, memberships, and private offices for founders, independent professionals, and small teams, plus member events and a startup resource library.

programs.name: ChicoSTART NextGen Incubator
programs.short: Semester-long incubator cohort for founders 18 and older, combining a startup curriculum with mentorship, technical advising, and collaborative workspace in Chico.

programs.name: CIDER Drone Pilot Training Program
programs.short: A selective program that trains UC Santa Cruz students to fly drones safely, with FAA Part 107 exam preparation, flight practice, GIS and photogrammetry, and group projects, including a dedicated agriculture track.

programs.name: CIDER Summer Drone Intensive Training
programs.short: Summer drone training for UC Santa Cruz undergraduate and graduate students, covering FAA Part 107 preparation, flight training, GIS and photogrammetry, and small-group research projects on the campus farm.

programs.name: Citrus Clonal Protection Program
programs.short: Disease-tested citrus varieties and clean budwood for California nurseries and growers.
programs.summary: UC Riverside-led program that maintains disease-tested citrus varieties, supplies clean budwood to nurseries and growers, and manages the introduction of new citrus varieties into California.

programs.name: Climate Smart Agriculture Technical Assistance
programs.short: One-on-one help for farmers and ranchers from CDFA-funded technical assistance providers and UC ANR Community Education Specialists, covering project design, conservation planning, grant writing, and project management.

providers.name: California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA)

programs.name: College of Agriculture Bachelor's Degrees
programs.short: Bachelor's degrees in Agricultural Business, Agricultural Science, Animal Science, and Plant and Soil Science (which has a Regenerative Agriculture option), with hands-on learning at the 800-acre University Farm.

programs.name: Commercialization Engine
programs.short: Connects growers and agtech companies through grower challenge workshops, an R&D library, market-entry preparation, and technology transfer support, helping field-ready solutions move toward adoption on farms.

programs.name: Community Food Ambassadors
programs.short: Course with a stipend on local food systems and healthy eating for Yolo County residents. Graduates can go on to work at CLBL's Mobile Farmers Market and promote local agriculture.

programs.name: CRARS Technical Assistance for Farmers and Ranchers
programs.short: Conservation and grazing plans, advice on practices such as cover crops and compost, and help applying for EQIP and Healthy Soils funding for northern California farmers and ranchers.

programs.name: CSTEM Professional Mentoring Program
programs.short: Pairs CSUSM STEM undergraduates with industry professionals for monthly mentoring on careers, interviews, resumes, networking, and graduate school.

programs.name: CSTEM Summer Scholars Program
programs.short: Paid summer research experience where CSUSM and local community college undergraduates work with a faculty mentor on STEM projects, with weekly seminars and a closing poster showcase.

programs.name: CSU Bakersfield Small Business Development Center
programs.short: One-on-one business advising, workshops and help finding capital for entrepreneurs and small businesses in Kern, Inyo and Mono counties, including agricultural and value-added food businesses.

programs.name: Culinary Catalyst
programs.short: One-week program for local food entrepreneurs combining HACCP food-safety certification training with workshops on business planning, pricing, financing, and working with local government.

programs.name: Diesel Farm Machinery and Heavy Equipment Technician (Certificate)
programs.short: Career technical certificate in maintaining and repairing farm tractors, agricultural hydraulic equipment, and other diesel and heavy machinery, preparing students for ASE diesel exams and jobs such as farm equipment technician.

programs.name: DRIVE Startup Incubator Network
programs.short: A network of thematically focused business incubators near the UC Davis campus offering shared office and lab space to early-stage UC Davis-affiliated startups.

programs.name: Drones Uplifting California Communities (DUCC)
programs.short: Educator training that expands access to drone skills and education through schools and colleges across California.
programs.summary: A train-the-trainer program that prepares educators, especially high school and community college instructors, to teach drone skills, combining online FAA Part 107 exam preparation, practical flight training and curriculum support so they can bring drone learning into their schools and colleges.

programs.name: Ecological Farming Technical Assistance
programs.short: On-farm technical assistance, field days, webinars, and research on ecological pest management, hedgerows, cover crops, compost, and soil health, including Healthy Soils Program application support.

programs.name: EDC Business Services
programs.short: Free, personalized help from the county's Economic Development Collaborative for Sonoma County businesses at any stage, covering startup steps, financing options, expansion, and finding employees.

programs.name: El Futuro Educational Scholarship
programs.short: Multi-year scholarship for Napa County residents pursuing an associate degree in viticulture and enology at Napa Valley College or Santa Rosa Junior College.

programs.name: Entrepreneurship Makerspace Boot Camp
programs.short: Nine-week evening course for aspiring business owners in Yolo County covering business fundamentals, marketing, finance, and permits, with ongoing coaching and access to the library's Square One makerspace.

programs.name: Equipment Lending Library
programs.short: Short-term loans of specialized, scale-appropriate farm tools and equipment from the Kearney research center, with required training and staff delivery, so small Central Valley farms can try technology before buying.

programs.name: Escondido AgX Regional Food Hub
programs.short: Planned food hub to aggregate and distribute locally grown produce, including organic goods, so small San Diego County farms can reach larger buyers and markets.

programs.name: Escondido AgX Regional Innovation Hub: Business Incubator and CPG Lab & Test Kitchen
programs.short: Planned incubator space and consumer packaged goods lab and test kitchen for agtech and food ventures at the Escondido hub.

programs.name: Escondido AgX Workforce Training & Development
programs.short: Planned training in agricultural technology, food systems, and climate-smart farming, built with regional employers to upskill current agricultural workers and open pathways into living-wage jobs.

programs.name: ExCITE Riverside Incubator
programs.short: Downtown Riverside incubator offering flexible coworking space, mentoring through UCR's EPIC Small Business Development Center, workshops, networking events, and funding-readiness support for early-stage startups, including agtech companies.

programs.name: Explore (Quest Club and Tech Studios)
programs.short: Career exploration for teens at Digital NEST centers, with hands-on design, AI, and coding workshops, real projects, and company visits that help members discover their interests.

programs.name: Extended Learning Agriculture Technology (Noncredit)
programs.short: Noncredit courses for adults and current workers, including an Ag Technology certificate on the fresh fruit industry, emerging agricultural technologies, and HACCP food safety, plus forklift, ag mechanics, and welding courses.

programs.name: F3 Innovate Catalyst Fund
programs.short: Outcome-based working capital, such as recoverable grants or revenue sharing, that helps growers, integrators, and technology providers test and put proven agricultural technologies into use at scale.

programs.name: F3i Supercomputing Center
programs.short: Regional AI and data-processing infrastructure for agricultural modeling and research, giving California agtech startups and researchers access to computing capacity and shared agricultural data through an online portal.

programs.name: Farm Business Incubator
programs.short: Land leases with shared infrastructure and ongoing mentoring in Yolo County for beginning farmers starting their own farm businesses, testing production methods and building markets.

programs.name: Farm Manager Apprenticeship
programs.short: State-registered apprenticeship that combines paid on-the-job training with participating farm employers, agricultural coursework and leadership development. It prepares agricultural workers for supervisor and manager roles.

programs.name: Farm Research and Innovation
programs.short: Connects Central Valley growers with UC researchers and product developers to run field trials, share farmer feedback with developers, and deliver hands-on training on irrigation, soil health, and crop management.

programs.name: Farm Robotics Academy
programs.short: Agricultural robotics learning and team support for high school and community college students.
programs.summary: Farm Robotics Academy supports agricultural technology learning for students, including high school and community college teams, through robotics, drones and artificial intelligence. UC ANR Innovate and regional partners provide educator, curriculum and team support.

providers.name: AI Institute for Next Generation Food Systems (AIFS)
UC ANR Hopland Research and Extension Center

programs.name: Farm Robotics Challenge
programs.short: Student agricultural robotics projects connected to agricultural innovation and workforce learning.
programs.summary: Farm Robotics Challenge is a student engineering and design competition led by UC ANR Innovate and the AI Institute for Next Generation Food Systems. Teams develop and test robotics and artificial intelligence solutions to agricultural problems, building practical technology and workforce skills.

providers.name: AI Institute for Next Generation Food Systems (AIFS)
UC ANR Hopland Research and Extension Center

programs.name: Farm to Market (Farm to Cafeteria and marketing support)
programs.short: Technical assistance, marketing classes, and farmer-buyer networking mixers that help family farms sell to schools, hospitals, universities, CSA members, and other buyers.

programs.name: FARMS Program
programs.short: Agricultural learning and field experiences connected to agriculture and natural resource careers.
programs.summary: The Center for Land-Based Learning’s FARMS program and field days connect agricultural learning with hands-on experiences and exploration of agriculture and natural resource careers.

programs.name: Farmworker Education and Advancement Program
programs.short: Technical agricultural courses for working farmworkers, taught in Spanish with English terminology, applied math, and workplace skills built in; includes Basic and Advanced Berry Horticulture courses with certificates of proficiency.

programs.name: Fee-for-Service Consulting
programs.short: Paid technical support from district staff in agricultural management and business, forestry, geology, grant writing, project development, environmental review, and water monitoring, available on request to producers, landowners, and agencies.

programs.name: FFA & 4-H Loans
programs.short: Low- or no-interest loans, offered with F&M Bank, that help Napa County 4-H, FFA and Grange youth cover start-up costs for animal and vocational projects.

programs.name: Food Entrepreneurship Academy (Business Launchpad)
programs.short: Training and coaching on business planning, licensing, food safety, and permitting for aspiring food entrepreneurs, especially mobile food vendors and cottage food operators, with connections to shared kitchens.

programs.name: Food Safety Services
programs.short: Workshops, webinars, one-on-one farm visits, plan templates, and audit preparation that help small and underserved farms meet food safety rules and Good Agricultural Practices, in English, Spanish, and Hmong.

programs.name: Fresh Success
programs.short: Education, training and employment support for CalFresh participants, delivered by participating community colleges, adult schools and community-based organizations and administered by the Foundation for California Community Colleges. Services can include classes, career counseling, job search and placement help, tutoring, case management, and help with costs such as transportation and textbooks.

programs.name: Global Cattle Innovation Platform
programs.short: A platform in its first phase that connects beef and dairy producers, entrepreneurs, researchers, and investors to identify challenges and offer technical validation and commercialization support for cattle innovations.

programs.name: Good Jobs Central Valley
programs.short: An employer-led Fresno EDC initiative offering free industry-designed training, pre-apprenticeship, internships, and support services that prepare Central Valley job seekers for careers in manufacturing, construction, logistics, and business services.

programs.name: Grimm Family Center Internships & Careers
programs.short: The Grimm Family Center links CSUB agriculture students to internship placements, center internships and career resources. It also works with agricultural employers who want to host interns.

programs.name: HARVEST AgTech
programs.short: Innovation platform giving selected agtech startups technical validation projects, lab work and field trials with university research partners, commercialization support, and connections to investors and corporate partners.

programs.name: Healthy Soils Program
programs.short: CDFA incentive grants and technical assistance that help California farmers and ranchers adopt soil health practices such as cover crops, compost, hedgerows, and reduced or no tillage.

providers.name: California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA)

programs.name: Healthy Soils Program Technical Assistance (Siskiyou County)
programs.short: No-cost technical assistance for Siskiyou County farmers and ranchers in a state-funded Healthy Soils grant program, from application support through design and implementation of soil health practices.

programs.name: Hopland Scholars Research Award
programs.short: Small awards that cover project fees and on-site lodging for undergraduate and graduate students conducting extended field research or extension projects at Hopland REC.

providers.name: UC ANR Hopland Research and Extension Center

programs.name: Horticulture (A.S. Degree and Certificates)
programs.short: Horticulture degree and certificates for students and green-industry workers, covering plant science, propagation, irrigation, pest management, nursery operations, and landscape design, with hands-on greenhouse, aquaponics, and orchard work.

programs.name: IBank Farm Loan Program
programs.short: Small farm loans made through participating Financial Development Corporations and backed by USDA Farm Service Agency guarantees, for small farms and ranches in California.

providers.name: California Governor’s Office of Business and Economic Development (GO-Biz)

programs.name: Ignition Grants
programs.short: Project funding and mentorship for middle and high school students building science fair projects on agriculture and food systems challenges, from research through a working prototype, guided by a science fair coach.

programs.name: Imperial Regional Alliance Internship to Career Program
programs.short: Internship placements that match Imperial Valley College and SDSU Imperial Valley students with local employers, giving students hands-on work experience and employers access to emerging talent.

programs.name: INNOVAR Entrepreneurial Training
programs.short: Seven-week Lean LaunchPad customer-discovery program in the NSF I-Corps Hub West that helps researchers, students, and regional innovators, including in sustainable farming, test whether their technology meets a real market need.

programs.name: Innovation Grants
programs.short: Competitive grants with mentorship, pilot coordination, and commercialization support for teams ready to field-test and validate agricultural technologies with growers and operators in the Central Valley.

programs.name: International Business Services
programs.short: Help for international companies entering or expanding in the Sacramento region, including site selection, incentives, research, hiring support, and connections to consulates, service providers and international investors.

programs.name: Invest in California (foreign direct investment services)
programs.short: Support for international companies and investors weighing California operations, including site selection help, wage, tax, and utility cost data, and networking with state and regional partners.

providers.name: California Governor’s Office of Business and Economic Development (GO-Biz)

programs.name: Irrigation and Nitrogen Management Training for Grower Self-Certification
programs.short: A self-paced online course and exam from CDFA's Fertilizer Research and Education Program that qualifies growers to self-certify irrigation and nitrogen management plans for their own operations.

providers.name: California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA)

programs.name: IVEDC Business Development Services
programs.short: Confidential help for companies, including agribusiness and food processors, locating or expanding in Imperial County, covering site selection, permitting, utilities, incentive and financing options, market analysis, and workforce connections.

programs.name: Jordan College of Agricultural Sciences and Technology Degree Programs
programs.short: Bachelor's and master's degrees, minors, and certificates in agricultural business, animal science, agricultural education, food science, plant science, viticulture and enology, and agricultural systems management, including a precision agriculture minor.

programs.name: Labor Market Data and Custom Research
programs.short: Fresno County labor market data, city economic profiles, and custom research on workforce availability, wage rates, major employers, and industries for businesses, investors, and site selectors.

programs.name: Lake Wildfire Resilience Workforce Program
programs.short: Wildland firefighter certification, fire and forestry career training, and paid on-the-job field training for Lake County residents. Training covers fuels reduction, land restoration, chainsaw operation and cultural fire practices.

providers.name: Workforce Alliance of the North Bay

programs.name: Land for Agriculture conservation easements
programs.short: Sonoma County Ag + Open Space buys conservation easements from willing owners of Sonoma County farms and ranches, or accepts them as donations, permanently protecting working agricultural land.

programs.name: Launch at BizzNEST
programs.short: Young adults apply to BizzNEST, Digital NEST's in-house creative agency, to work on paid client projects with mentorship, resume coaching, and interview preparation.

programs.name: Leadership Program (CULTIVAR and Women's Leadership Workshop)
programs.short: Leadership development for emerging vineyard leaders through the CULTIVAR and CULTIVAR360 academies and a women's leadership workshop, building communication, decision-making, and team skills.

programs.name: Learning to Lead (L2L) Program
programs.short: USDA-funded program for IVC agriculture majors offering paid internships with agencies and local ag employers, leadership conferences, counseling and workshops, and scholarships for transfer to partner universities.

programs.name: Local Food for Schools (Ventura County School Food Hub)
programs.short: School food hub, run with Farm Cart Organics, that sources produce from local farms and delivers it to Ventura County school meal programs, giving growers a route into school food markets.

programs.name: Local Food Marketing Assistance
programs.short: Marketing support that raises the visibility of local food businesses through regional branding, pop-ups, social media campaigns, and introductions to retailers and institutions.

programs.name: Management Program (Supervisor Development Series)
programs.short: Experiential training for vineyard supervisors and emerging managers on communication, accountability, problem-solving, and day-to-day management tools, delivered through a supervisor development series and field trips.

programs.name: Mechanized Agriculture (Equipment Service Technician) Program
programs.short: Associate degree and certificates that train equipment service technicians on engines, transmissions, hydraulics, and electrical systems in dealer-style labs, supported by Quinn Company, the regional Caterpillar dealer.

programs.name: Mechanized Agriculture Technology
programs.short: An associate degree and certificates in agricultural equipment, diesel engines, hydraulics and power equipment. It prepares students for technician jobs and helps working farmers and technicians update their skills.

programs.name: Napa Green Vineyard Certification
programs.short: Third-party-verified regenerative and climate-focused certification for Napa County vineyards, including a custom carbon farm plan, irrigation efficiency assessment, expert consulting, and audits every three years.

programs.name: Napa Green Winery Certification
programs.short: Third-party sustainability certification for Napa Valley wineries, with an integrated assessment of energy, water, materials, and emissions, improvement planning, and standards covering social equity and supply chain.

programs.name: Napa One Block Challenge
programs.short: Peer-learning program where Napa County winegrowers pilot four stacked regenerative practices on one vineyard block, track soil health, and join field days every few months.

programs.name: Napa VC Early-Stage Venture Investment
programs.short: Seed through Series A investment, with recruiting, go-to-market, and follow-on financing support, for startups in vineyard robotics and automation, wine and hospitality technology, and data intelligence.

programs.name: Nature-Based Solutions Certificate Courses
programs.short: Hands-on certificate courses in regenerative landscaping and gardening, composting, biochar, vermiculture, fungi-based bioremediation, and habitat restoration, plus vocational training in regenerative food service and logistics.

programs.name: NexTech Robotics
programs.short: A free robotics and coding program for San Joaquin Valley middle and high school students, taught by UC Merced near-peer mentors and using real ag-tech research case studies to show robotics in agriculture.

programs.name: North Valley Food Hub
programs.short: Online wholesale marketplace and distribution hub, run by Chico State's Center for Regenerative Agriculture and Resilient Systems, that helps northern California farmers sell local food to institutions and other buyers.

programs.name: NSF I-Corps at UC Davis (Regional Customer Discovery Course)
programs.short: A remote customer-discovery course where teams with a technology-based startup idea interview potential customers to test their business model; UC Davis runs agtech-focused cohorts.

programs.name: NSF I-Corps ZAP Program (Hub West)
programs.short: Short virtual customer-discovery program for science and engineering innovators, offered through the NSF I-Corps Hub West, with a path toward the national I-Corps Teams program.

programs.name: Nutrition Education
programs.short: Cooking classes and garden-based nutrition lessons that use seasonal local produce to teach Ventura County students about healthy food and where it comes from.

programs.name: NVV Leadership Program
programs.short: A nine-month cohort program for Napa Valley wine industry professionals, combining in-person sessions, speakers, readings, and a group project addressing an industry or community need.

programs.name: Organic Certification Support
programs.short: One-on-one technical assistance, mentor matching with experienced organic growers, field days, and a certifier comparison tool for California farmers transitioning to or renewing organic certification.

programs.name: Patrick Foley Fields of Opportunity (Summer Mentor and Apprentice Programs)
programs.short: Mentorship pathway pairing participants with wine-industry mentors through an eight-week summer program, an apprentice track with career workshops, and an alumni network supporting vineyard career growth.

programs.name: Peer-to-Peer Learning Circles (Mujeres en Accion)
programs.short: Participant-led groups where women in Monterey and Santa Cruz counties set personal goals and build leadership, with topics such as education, training, childcare access, and pathways to better-paying jobs.

providers.name: Action Council and Mujeres en Acción

programs.name: Permit and Regulatory Assistance (including CalGold)
programs.short: Guidance for businesses of any size on registering, identifying required federal, state, regional, and local permits and licenses, and staying in compliance, backed by the CalGold permit lookup tool.

providers.name: California Governor’s Office of Business and Economic Development (GO-Biz)

programs.name: Plant and Soil Science Program
programs.short: Transfer and associate degrees plus certificates for irrigation, fertility, and pest management technicians, plant protection interns, and pest control advisor preparation, using the college's 300-acre school farm and greenhouses.

programs.name: Plug and Play Agtech Accelerator (Topeka)
programs.short: Agtech accelerator run from Plug and Play's Topeka, Kansas location connecting startups in automation, analytics, field monitoring, precision farming, and supply chain with agri-food corporate partners.

programs.name: Plug and Play Investment Opportunities
programs.short: Plug and Play's in-house venture team invests in startups across stages, mostly seed, and connects portfolio companies with co-investors, mentors, and corporate pilot partners.

programs.name: Plug and Play Silicon Valley Co-Working
programs.short: Furnished private offices and shared desks for founders and growing teams at Plug and Play's Silicon Valley sites in Sunnyvale, Palo Alto, Redwood City and San Jose, with amenities that vary by site. Tenants also get access to Plug and Play events, mentorship opportunities and a community of startups, investors and corporate partners.

programs.name: Pre-Seed and Seed Investment
programs.short: Early-stage venture investment for U.S. agtech startups whose technologies support the future of agricultural work and farmworker well-being; founders submit their company through an online form.

programs.name: Quarter at Aggie Square: Plants, People and the Planet
programs.short: A quarter-long experience pairing a community engagement course with a Sacramento-area internship, where UC Davis undergraduates of any major explore food systems, agriculture, and sustainability.

programs.name: Raley's Food Lab
programs.short: A certified commercial kitchen at AgStart, reserved by the hour, where food entrepreneurs and product developers create ingredients and recipes and prototype new food products.

programs.name: Regenerating Napa Grant
programs.short: Practice payments for Napa-area growers who implement regenerative practices such as cover crops, compost, biochar, hedgerows, no-till, and rotational grazing, with Napa Green guiding applications and documentation.

programs.name: Regenerative Agriculture Farm Demonstration Network
programs.short: A network of mentor farms and demonstration sites, with field days, where Northern California farmers and ranchers see regenerative and climate-smart practices in use and can request technical assistance.

programs.name: Regenerative Agriculture Interdisciplinary Studies MS
programs.short: In-person graduate program in regenerative agriculture. Students design an interdisciplinary course plan and do research at the University Farm and Chico State's Regenerative Agriculture Demonstration Lab.

programs.name: Region 2 Vineyard Permit Group Program
programs.short: Group enrollment that helps Napa River watershed vineyards meet the regional water board's Vineyard General Permit. The Farm Bureau collects fees and runs group water-quality monitoring for enrolled properties.

programs.name: Reservoir Co
programs.short: Technical tools for agricultural robotics and artificial intelligence.
programs.summary: Reservoir Co provides agricultural technology startups with APIs, data, hardware and developer tools for autonomy, robotics, precision technology and artificial intelligence.

programs.name: Reservoir Farms
programs.short: Working-farm incubation, field trials, advising and shared facilities.
programs.summary: Reservoir Farms provides working-farm incubators where agricultural technology startups develop and validate products through field trials, grower feedback, advising, and access to land, workshops and workspace.

upcoming.t: Organic Grower Summit reception and field demos

programs.name: Reservoir VC
programs.short: Venture investment in agricultural robotics and artificial intelligence.
programs.summary: Reservoir VC invests in early-stage agricultural robotics and artificial intelligence startups developing technologies for demanding field conditions.

programs.name: Resilient Entrepreneur Program
programs.short: A multi-month program for aspiring and early-stage entrepreneurs combining a Saturday business bootcamp, one-on-one mentoring, and support from business students, with a focus on underinvested communities.

programs.name: RIoT Labs Prototyping and Wireless Testing
programs.short: Engineering support for connected-device startups, including agtech, with prototyping, technology validation, radio-frequency testing, and device certification help through RIoT Labs and the Wireless Research Center in North Carolina.

programs.name: Safety Program
programs.short: Hands-on safety training built for vineyard conditions, covering first aid and CPR, tractor and equipment safety, pesticide safety, night-harvest protocols, and harassment prevention for vineyard crews.

programs.name: SBIR Phase I Workshop
programs.short: Six-week team workshop combining customer discovery, entrepreneur-in-residence mentoring, and commercialization planning for companies and innovators preparing federal SBIR or STTR Phase I proposals.

programs.name: SCALE Small Business Centers Network
programs.short: Statewide network of small business centers offering no-cost one-on-one advising, low-cost training, and help connecting with lenders, in person or virtually.

providers.name: California Governor’s Office of Business and Economic Development (GO-Biz)

programs.name: SF-ADAPT Conference Stipends for Small Farmers
programs.short: Stipends and support that help small farmers attend major agricultural and technology conferences, where they can learn about new tools and connect with peers, researchers, and developers.

programs.name: SF-ADAPT Innovation Connection
programs.short: Connects small and medium-scale farmers with technology developers and researchers to co-create tools and run on-farm trials and pilot projects, with testing and equipment demonstrations at Kearney REC.

programs.name: Sheep Shearing and Care Classes
programs.short: Small-group, hands-on classes using the center's research flock, including Lambing School, Sheep Shearing and Basic Care 101, Technique Refinement, and crutching and wigging, for people who run or work with sheep.

providers.name: UC ANR Hopland Research and Extension Center

programs.name: Silicon Valley Food & Beverage Innovation Platform
programs.short: Corporate-partnered accelerator program at Plug and Play's Sunnyvale headquarters connecting food, beverage, and farm-to-table technology startups with major food companies for pilots and business development.

programs.name: Siskiyou Mobile Irrigation Lab on-farm irrigation assessments
programs.short: On-farm irrigation system assessments, water-use efficiency tools and technical support for Siskiyou County producers, delivered by trained irrigation technicians.

programs.name: Siskiyou Prescribed Burn Association
programs.short: Community prescribed burn association, co-sponsored by the district, that offers burn consultations, equipment, and help conducting prescribed burns for Siskiyou County landowners, and has offered public burn trainings.

programs.name: SLEWS Program
programs.short: High school students restore habitat on a farm or ranch over several field days, planting native vegetation and learning about conservation careers alongside mentors and landowners.

programs.name: Small Farm Food Aggregation Hubs
programs.short: Aggregation hubs that combine products from small farms and food businesses for coordinated distribution to schools, hospitals, and grocers, helping producers reach institutional and wholesale buyers.

programs.name: Small Farm Tech Hub
programs.short: One-on-one consultations, guides, workshops, and peer communities that help small farms, farmers markets, and food hubs adopt e-commerce, point-of-sale, digital marketing, and other appropriate technology.

programs.name: Specialty Crop Block Grant Program
programs.short: CDFA's annual competitive grants for projects that make California fruits, vegetables, tree nuts, and nursery crops more competitive. Industry groups, businesses, nonprofits, tribes, agencies, and colleges can apply; individual farmers cannot.

providers.name: California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA)

programs.name: STAIR Grant Program
programs.short: Proof-of-concept seed grants, industry mentoring, and entrepreneurial training that help UC Davis researchers move early-stage inventions, including food and agriculture technologies, toward licensing or a startup.

programs.name: START Program
programs.short: Startup formation support for UC Davis-affiliated founders commercializing university research, including pitch coaching, grant workshops, legal and service-provider connections, mentors, market reports, and entrepreneur-in-residence advice.

programs.name: State Water Efficiency and Enhancement Program (SWEEP)
programs.short: CDFA grants that help farmers and ranchers install water- and energy-saving irrigation upgrades, such as soil moisture monitoring, drip systems, pump improvements, and renewable energy for pumping.

providers.name: California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA)

programs.name: Student Research Scholars Program
programs.short: Year-long program pairing CSUB students with faculty mentors on research for the agriculture industry. It includes scholarship support and a spring research symposium.

programs.name: Student Training & Employment Program (STEP)
programs.short: Paid work experience and job preparation for California students with disabilities ages 16 to 21, coordinated by the California Department of Rehabilitation and the Foundation for California Community Colleges and delivered through local workforce development boards. Students build workplace readiness and self-advocacy skills, explore careers and get counseling on education after high school.

programs.name: SVG Ventures Pioneer Fund
programs.short: SVG Ventures fund that invests in seed to Series A agrifood tech startups across biotech, food, supply chain, digital farming and sustainability.

programs.name: Technical Assistance Program (TAP)
programs.short: One-on-one, confidential advising, technical assistance, and training for entrepreneurs and small business owners starting or expanding a business in the North State.

programs.name: Technical Assistance Provider (TAP) Certification and Regenerative Agriculture Professional Courses
programs.short: Online professional courses from Chico State's Center for Regenerative Agriculture on soil health, grazing, farm planning and conservation. Take single courses, or complete four for TAP certification.

programs.name: Technology Innovation and Evaluation (TIE) Program
programs.short: Expert committee review and guidance for inventors and entrepreneurs developing water, energy, and agriculture technologies, helping them move toward commercialization and reach funding resources through BlueTechValley.

programs.name: TerraTech Summer Internship
programs.short: A paid summer internship placing undergraduate and graduate students with Central Valley companies, startups, nonprofits, and public agencies on food and agriculture projects in AI, data science, automation, robotics, and sustainability.

programs.name: The Lab@AgStart
programs.short: Shared wet-lab benches, fermentation and tissue-culture labs, co-working, offices, and meeting space in Woodland for agriculture, food, and health startups doing bench-level commercialization.

programs.name: The Plant
programs.short: Planned innovation campus at the Port of West Sacramento with wet labs, biomanufacturing, controlled-environment agriculture, food innovation and incubation space for startups and researchers scaling food and agriculture technologies.

providers.name: UC Agriculture and Natural Resources (UC ANR)

programs.name: The Source Smart Agriculture Testbed
programs.short: Greenhouse and high-tunnel testbed in Wilson, North Carolina, where agtech startups, growers, and researchers trial sensors, AI, data tools, autonomous equipment, crops, and growing methods in real conditions.

programs.name: THRIVE Global Impact Accelerator Program
programs.short: Accelerator for Series A+ agrifood, climate and energy tech companies chosen from top Global Impact Challenge applicants. It offers virtual programming, mentorship and an in-person week in Silicon Valley.

programs.name: THRIVE Studio Sprint
programs.short: Six-week virtual program that helps researchers and first-time founders take an agrifood tech idea to a defined minimum viable product through customer discovery, expert advice and learning alongside a cohort.

programs.name: UC ANR Build
programs.short: Support for early agricultural technology development.
programs.summary: UC ANR Build supports early agricultural technology development through prototype development, market evaluation and early commercialization strategy within UC ANR Innovate.

programs.name: UC ANR Connect
programs.short: Grower-informed commercialization connections and agricultural technology field demonstrations.
programs.summary: UC ANR Connect links agricultural technology companies with grower-informed commercialization and field demonstration through UC ANR Innovate, in partnership with Farmhand Ventures.

programs.name: UC ANR Research and Extension Centers
programs.short: Nine UC field research stations across California's farming regions. Researchers and agtech companies working with a UC collaborator run field trials there, and growers attend field days and workshops.

providers.name: UC Agriculture and Natural Resources (UC ANR)

programs.name: UC Cooperative Extension
programs.short: County-based UC advisors and specialists who give farmers, ranchers and agricultural businesses research-based guidance, local field trials, workshops and field days.

providers.name: UC Agriculture and Natural Resources (UC ANR)

programs.name: UC Davis Continuing and Professional Education Agriculture Programs
programs.short: Professional certificates and courses for farmers, industry professionals, and career changers, including viticulture, winemaking, master brewers, nuts and tree fruit education, sensory science, and wine business.

programs.name: UC IPM Online Training
programs.short: Free self-paced online courses from the UC Statewide IPM Program on pest management, pesticide application and safety.

providers.name: UC Agriculture and Natural Resources (UC ANR)

programs.name: UC Merced Experimental Smart Farm Research Support
programs.short: UC Merced's 40-acre Experimental Smart Farm gives researchers instrumented field plots, greenhouse space, sensor networks, drones and data systems, along with field, engineering and data science support. Agtech companies can also arrange pilot projects, data collection and product validation on the farm through UC Merced's VISTA F3 program.

programs.name: UCR Available Technologies (Technology Licensing)
programs.short: Searchable portfolio of more than 500 UC Riverside inventions, including patented plant varieties such as avocado, citrus, and asparagus, that companies and founders can license or develop through research partnerships.

programs.name: Unmanned Aircraft Systems Certificate of Achievement
programs.short: A for-credit Orange Coast College certificate covering drone systems, automation, electronics, and photogrammetry that prepares students for FAA Part 107 remote pilot work, including agricultural uses like crop scouting and irrigation.

programs.name: Urban Ag Internship Program
programs.short: Year-long paid internship for Sacramento high school students. It combines school garden work, workforce development classes, farm field trips and guest speakers on agriculture and environmental careers.

programs.name: Valley Ventures
programs.short: Mostly online accelerator for later-stage agtech startups, with sales and pitch training, mentoring from founders and industry leaders, investor education, and Central Valley farm tours.

programs.name: Vineyard and Winery Local Certificates
programs.short: Short local certificates, such as Vineyard Pest Scout, Viticulture Operations, and Wine Laboratory Technician, that build specific job skills for entry-level and current vineyard and winery workers.

programs.name: Viticulture & Winery Technology Work Experience (WOEX)
programs.short: Students earn college credit for supervised paid or volunteer work at vineyards and wineries, setting learning objectives with their job supervisor and instructor.

programs.name: Viticulture (A.S.)
programs.short: Associate degree for students preparing for vineyard careers, combining grape-growing coursework with hands-on practice in the college's five-acre teaching vineyard.

programs.name: Viticulture and Enology (Certificate of Achievement)
programs.short: Certificate combining core vineyard and winemaking coursework for students and working professionals who want a focused wine-industry credential without completing a full associate degree.

programs.name: Viticulture Program
programs.short: Field days, workshops, and certification prep classes on pruning, canopy management, irrigation, climate, wildfire risk, and vineyard technology for vineyard workers, including the annual Napa County Pruning Contest.

programs.name: Western Center for Agricultural Health and Safety Trainings
programs.short: Interactive English and Spanish trainings on heat illness prevention, wildfire smoke, injury and illness prevention plans, and frontline supervisor safety leadership for farmworkers, crew leaders, and agricultural employers.

programs.name: Western Growers Center for Innovation & Technology
programs.short: Connections between agricultural technology companies, growers, and shippers for feedback and field testing.
programs.summary: Western Growers' innovation center connects agtech startups with fresh produce growers and shippers for feedback, field testing, and industry connections, including sponsored residencies at Reservoir Farms in Salinas.

programs.name: Western Growers University
programs.short: Professional development covering leadership, supervisory skills, employment law, safety, and food safety.
programs.summary: Bilingual professional development for farming operations and ag businesses, including supervisory and leadership training, HR and employment law, compliance, safety, and food safety, offered as webinars and onsite training.

programs.name: Wine Marketing and Sales (A.S. and Certificate of Achievement)
programs.short: Associate degree and certificate covering the business side of wine, including marketing and sales, for students and wine-industry employees moving into sales, marketing, or hospitality roles.

programs.name: Wine Production (Certificate of Achievement)
programs.short: Certificate of production-oriented courses in viticulture and winemaking, including lab analysis, sensory evaluation, and cellar operations. A distance-education option for working professionals has paired online courses with an on-campus winery intensive.

programs.name: Winemaking (A.S.)
programs.short: Associate degree in winemaking for students preparing for cellar, lab, and production roles, with practical training in the college's bonded teaching winery.

programs.name: Workforce Resources (New Employment Opportunities Program)
programs.short: Connects Fresno County employers with customized training, hiring incentives, and the County's New Employment Opportunities program, which offers screened job-ready candidates, specialized training, retention support, and wage subsidies.

programs.name: Workplace Training Program
programs.short: Practical workshops on communication, teamwork, collaboration, and employee engagement that help vineyard crews and supervisors build healthier, more positive workplaces.

programs.name: Wrap Around Business Services
programs.short: One-on-one consulting for food entrepreneurs on licensing and permits, product development, food safety compliance, marketing, and funding navigation, with continued support as businesses grow.

programs.name: Youth Innovators Lab
programs.short: Entrepreneurship program for teens ages 16 to 18, run alongside the NextGen incubator, that helps young people turn ideas for solving real-world problems into concrete plans.
